claim: In the founding trap-tube study only 3 of 6 crows learned the task (mean 103.3 trials), all 3 passed cue-removal transfers and the trap-table, and all 3 failed the two-hole transfer; the pass was keyed to the hole, not the trap base.
agent_test: For each pass, build a near variant where the surface feature and the true cause split (two-hole analogue). Score the variant at equal tokens against the original.

claim: A far visual transfer pass (trap-table) can coexist with failure on a near structural variant, so one transfer pass does not show the deep rule; only learners passed, so the transfer came from tube experience. Rooks (7 of 8 solved, 6 of 7 failed far transfer), Darwin's finches (none transferred) and hooded crows (concrete rules) show the same pass-then-fail shape, though no one has repeated the exact two-hole test.
agent_test: Run both a far-surface twin and a near-structure twin of each pass test; require both.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Task format changes pass rates sharply within and across species (apes pull vs push, single tool vs rake, crow string vs metatool, breeze weight inference), so one failed probe is weak evidence of a capacity limit.
agent_test: Before recording a limit, rerun the probe in at least one differently built format (different wording, output budget, tool use) and log both.

claim: Crows' success can come from a cheaper contact rule than the one credited: stone-dropping innovators ignored weight, yet the same species used wind motion to infer weight in another paradigm.
agent_test: Identify an error signature that separates cheap rule from rich rule (the weight-inattention test) and check for it directly in agent outputs.

claim: Corvid Aesop's-fable performance is largely trial-and-error: gains come from rewarded outcomes, not errors, with no transfer between task variants; the apparent U-tube pass was a colour cue. Hennefield numbers now verified from PMC: after an efficient choice OR 5.00 (water vs sand, N=22), after an inefficient one OR 0.67, p=.08; task-order OR 0.81, p=.22.
agent_test: Log per-attempt learning curves in agent retry loops and test whether failed attempts change later behaviour at equal tokens.

claim: Apes can solve two functionally equivalent trap tasks yet show no correlation or transfer across them (r=0.13); removing the tool constraint raised success in chimpanzees.
agent_test: Check that a failed transfer is not caused by the interface; compare same-structure tasks in two interfaces.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Physical-cognition claims rest on tiny samples (median 7 animals, median 3 passers, 15 of 87 experiments with zero passers, positive claims 44-59%), so N=3 pass stories are hypotheses.
agent_test: Use many items and several seeds per probe; report per-item pass counts, not a single run.

claim: LLMs that pass default forms drop on counterfactual or altered same-structure forms (counterfactual tasks, altered alphabets, GSM-Symbolic, Corr2Cause paraphrase, ToM alterations) even when rule comprehension checks pass. 2024 reasoning models also drop (o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1 on GSM-NoOp); see K21 for how much of that is a lost rule.
agent_test: Pair every gated test with a counterfactual twin plus a rule-comprehension control; accept a scaffold gain only if it holds on the twin at equal tokens.

claim: Task-specific fine-tuning or RL in vision-language models raises in-domain physics accuracy but does not transfer to related tasks or styles.
agent_test: Not directly testable (we do not train); use as a warning that a prompt tuned on one probe family may not carry to another.

claim: Multimodal LLMs and VLMs stay below humans or near chance on intuitive physics and perceived causation; prompting (CoT, in-context expert example) does not rescue them.
agent_test: For physical-world questions give the agent a code simulator or tool and compare to prompting alone at equal tokens.

claim: Poor scores in embodied animal-style LLM tests may reflect the control interface and floor effects rather than reasoning; RL agents also stall on the causal levels. Exact per-level LLM scores are only in figures (12 trials per level); no tool-API rerun was found.
agent_test: Log whether each failure is perception, control or reasoning before writing a limit.

claim: Right answers do not imply right reasoning: only up to 11% of TRIP items had correct physical states and conflict identified though end accuracy reached 78%; vision encoders hold plausibility information the language model fails to use.
agent_test: Check intermediate claims in code, not only the final answer; compare end accuracy with chain validity.

claim: Reasoning-model collapse on puzzles is partly a probe artefact (output token limits, unsolvable instances, scoring), so a limit curve needs budget, solvability and scoring checks.
agent_test: For each limit curve confirm the output budget, solvability and scorer before recording it; ask for a generating program instead of full enumeration.

claim: LLM causal competence is split: strong on text causal benchmarks (97% pairwise, 92% CRASS, 98.5% post-cutoff) but weak on new structures (GPT-3 causal chain, Corr2Cause near random), with retrieval a rival explanation.
agent_test: Test with novel causal structures and renamed variables, not famous vignettes.

claim: Letting a model run its own experiments helps on easy structures but not on conjunctive rules; an experiment-then-act strategy can transfer when prompts carry explanations. Samiei 2026 tested LLMs only in the active condition, so it gives no equal-token passive contrast.
agent_test: Compare intervention-first with answer-first on blicket-style tasks at equal tokens, with a code-counted test budget.

claim: A step-wise feasibility self-check helped GPT-4 on unconventional tool-use problems but not Llama 2; LLM success is 35-42% vs 65.1% for people.
agent_test: Add a feasibility check pass per step and measure the change in wrong-tool errors at equal tokens.

claim: Competence can appear in passive looking-time tests (rooks, support relations) while failing in action tests; probe format matters in both directions.
agent_test: Test the same concept as a recognition judgement and as a generated action plan.

claim: Controls decide a pass: the inverted-tube control fails on humans too, the hidden-agent crow result was disputed for unbalanced controls, and a hole-avoidance habit was not excluded in the founding study.
agent_test: Validate each control on a known good reasoner before using it to grade the agent.

claim: A close replication of the breeze weight-inference task in kea failed (first touch 50% fan on vs 40% fan off, chi2=1.775, p=0.187), while crows passed (72.9% vs 47.9%).
agent_test: Run one capacity probe on several models and do not generalise from one.

claim: Methods checklists exist for AI cognition tests: avoid over-claiming and under-claiming (auxiliary oversight vs mechanistic chauvinism), use controls, test alternative strategies, strip cues.
agent_test: Adopt the checklist as an audit gate before any limit or gain enters the schema.

claim: Reasoning-era models still drop on one-clause or suffix twins (o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1 points on GSM-NoOp; R1 attack success 4.50% vs 1.50% random), but a 2026 audit found that after keeping only truly irrelevant clauses (12.4% of 945) the drop was 0-2 points. Much of the reported drop is distractor ambiguity, not a lost rule. Altered-alphabet and counterfactual twins have no 2025-2026 reasoning-model run in the sources found.
agent_test: Build each twin, have two auditors confirm the answer is unchanged, then report the drop only on audited twins; add a comprehension probe per twin.

claim: Prompting scaffolds keep their absolute gain on perturbed twins but do not close the seed-twin gap: GPT-3.5 COMP+SC 80.00 -> 69.47 vs CoT 74.17 -> 62.92 (gaps 10.53 vs 11.25); on GSM-IC, self-consistency lifted micro accuracy to 88.1-93.4% yet best macro accuracy was 45%.
agent_test: Run scaffold and plain arms on seeds and audited twins at equal tokens; report twin gain, seed-twin gap and macro accuracy (all twins of a seed right). Both sources use 2023-2024 models and unequal tokens.

claim: The two-hole result itself has not been repeated by anyone. Nearby trap-tube studies from other labs (rooks 7 of 8 solved, 6 of 7 failed far transfer; 3 of 7 rooks, 0 passed; finches 0 transferred) show the same pass-then-fail shape, but the exact two-hole transfer with crows has no independent replication found.
agent_test: Treat the pattern (pass, then fail a transfer that removes the visual constant) as the test shape, not the single two-hole item. Evidence is abstract-only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 0 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Some error signatures can be counted by running code: adoption of a misleading comment or print message (CodeCrash: -23.2% direct, -13.8% with CoT; reasoning models use 2-3x tokens on a plausible wrong hint) and applying an operation for an irrelevant quantity (GSM-NoOp o1-preview case). No paper reports a rate of hint adoption versus wrong-for-other-reasons, so the signature is proposed, not validated.
agent_test: Plant a wrong claim next to code or a problem, run the program, and count answers equal to the planted claim and not to the executed output; compare to the rate of other wrong answers.

claim: A premature or uncorrected first answer is the nearest LLM analogue of the crows' inhibition failure: models in multi-turn tasks drop 39% on average with +112% unreliability and do not recover from a wrong turn, and models miss their own errors 64.5% more than identical external ones (14 open non-reasoning models). Appending 'Wait' cut the blind spot 89.3%, so a cheap recheck gate works in that setting.
agent_test: Add a forced recheck turn after the first answer and score fixes on matched own-vs-other injected errors at equal tokens. Sources cover non-reasoning models and injected errors, not natural retry loops.

claim: No study was found that runs an LLM with a test-before-answer arm against a no-test arm at equal tokens on conjunctive rules. Samiei 2026 only has active LLM runs (6 models, 288 trials); Lampinen 2023 (c18) points to transfer only with explanations.
agent_test: Run the planned experiment: same conjunctive items, test-first vs answer-first arms, same token cap, score exact rule and objects.

claim: Mecattaf's exact per-level LLM accuracies are only in figures (12 trials per level, 59 children as reference); the paper blames the action-script control and a 30-script cap for part of the floor. No follow-up that gives a tool API was found, so whether an API lifts the causal levels is unknown.
agent_test: Do not cite per-level numbers. If we rebuild a causal level, offer the same tasks through a tool API and through free text and compare.

claim: Corvid learning-from-success can be measured per attempt as the odds of repeating the efficient choice after an efficient vs an inefficient previous choice (OR 5.00 vs 0.67 in water vs sand, N=22). No LLM retry-loop study applying this was found, so whether LLMs show it is unknown; chimpanzees and young children also gain little from seeing errors.
agent_test: In per-attempt logs of retry loops, fit the odds of repeating the correct strategy by previous outcome; test whether showing the failed attempt (with the reason) changes it.
